builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: GUMPIM: Unitary and Malleable Memory for Processing-in-Memory with Guaranteed PIM Pages
summary: GUMPIM replaces PIM memory management that either isolates PIM regions or disables memory interleaving, instead letting interleaved CPU pages and contiguous non-interleaved PIM pages coexist in one address space with zero-copy offloading. The cost is new DRAM-side interface hardware for dynamic address mapping plus OS-level dual-track page allocation, translation, and PIM-assisted page migration, with claims validated only on simulated or prototype PIM platforms. It can fail in practice because PIM-enabled HBM/LPDDR hardware is not commercially available at scale, the gains are confined to PIM-suitable workloads, and the technique does not touch GPU or API-based inference at all.
rationale: This is a hardware and memory-system design for DRAM processing-in-memory platforms, which the reader neither owns nor can procure, and it offers no mechanism applicable to single-GPU or API-based ML production.
technique: Dual-track memory management for DRAM PIM pages

claims.statement: GUMPIM replaces PIM memory management that either isolates PIM regions or disables memory interleaving, instead letting interleaved CPU pages and contiguous non-interleaved PIM pages coexist in one address space with zero-copy offloading. The cost is new DRAM-side interface hardware for dynamic address mapping plus OS-level dual-track page allocation, translation, and PIM-assisted page migration, with claims validated only on simulated or prototype PIM platforms. It can fail in practice because PIM-enabled HBM/LPDDR hardware is not commercially available at scale, the gains are confined to PIM-suitable workloads, and the technique does not touch GPU or API-based inference at all.
End-to-end 2.3x speedup over a state-of-the-art PIM baseline, with 2.7x lower memory allocation time, 4.93x lower CPU-part computation time, and under 0.1% CPU workload degradation.
